title: Cubism: Picasso and Braque
welcome_lead: Multiple viewpoints, one canvas — the shattering of single-point perspective.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: Cubism, Picasso, Braque, and the avant-garde.
final_note: I paint objects as I think them, not as I see them.

concepts.def: Avant-garde movement (1907-1914) fragmenting form into facets.
1912-1914 phase: brighter colour, collage, papier collé.

walkthroughs.body_html: Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (1907) merged influences from Iberian sculpture, African masks and Cézanne. Braque saw it that autumn; the partnership of Cubism began.
Analytical Cubism (1909-1912) dissected objects into faceted, muted near-abstractions. Synthetic Cubism (1912-1914) reassembled them with collage, papier collé and brighter colour.
Cubism abandoned the single-point perspective inherited from Alberti, presenting an object from several viewpoints at once — a structural revolution that opened modern art.
